To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the most discriminating feature for the normal class in KDD 09 training data is the number of failed login attempts, for the probe class is the number of root shell accesses, for the DoS class is the number and duration of connections to the host, and for the U2R class is the number root shell accesses.

(i) the most discriminative features for normal and DoS attacks are similar and are related to protocol, service and flags; (ii) the most discriminating feature for probe attacks is the number of failed logins; (iii) the most discriminant feature for R2L attacks is the number failed logins; and (iv) the most discrimant features for U2R attacks are the protocol and service.

the features that are most discriminating for each class in the KDD 99 datasets are: • For the class normal, the most discriminating feature is the number of failed login attempts in the last 2 hours.

In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the features in KDD 09 datasets do not discriminate between the different classes.
, the features in the KDD 99 dataset are highly correlated with the class labels and are relevant for the intrusion detection task.
, the features in KDD 09 dataset are not relevant to the task of anomaly and intrusion detection.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the features that are most discriminative for each class are different and the most discriminative features for one class are not necessarily the most discriminative for another class.
most of the features are irrelevant and only a handful of features are relevant to each class.

the most discriminating and relevant features for normal and DoS classes are the number of failed login attempts, the number of failed logins per connection and the number of connections, respectively.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the features in KDD 09 intrusion detection datasets are not relevant for the detection of intrusions.
the features are not equally relevant and some of them are not even useful.
, the most discriminating feature for each class does not necessarily have to be the same.
